parsed.basis: Transgender visitors to Moxico, in eastern Angola, face the national regime under which same-sex conduct was decriminalised in 2021 and discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation is punishable, although gender identity is not an enumerated constitutional ground and Angolan organisations report formal protection is not matched in practice. No entry rules specific to trans travellers and no dedicated shelters or facilities are recorded. Moxico is a sparsely populated, largely rural province far from Luanda, where courts, health services and advocacy organisations are concentrated, so recourse, emergency care and safe accommodation would be harder if a visitor were outed there. No documented local targeting campaign or protective infrastructure is known to distinguish it beyond remoteness and limited services.
